sentences.text: Palvennia was a medium-sized ichthyosaur reaching lengths of 3 to 4 meters.
Its snout was notably short, measuring about 0.6 times the total skull length.
The skull possessed a very large eye socket, which accounts for roughly 0.34 of the skull length.
Fossils were found in 2004 within the Agardhfjellet Formation on Spitsbergen.
The genus name honors PalVenn, the group of friends behind the Oslo museum expedition that uncovered the type specimen.
The holotype, cataloged as SVB 1451, retains nearly complete front skeletal parts and a skull.
Palvennia belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Its parent group is identified as Ophthalmosaurinae.
This animal lived in Central Spitsbergen, Norway, during the uppermost Jurassic period.
In 2019, researchers debated whether Palvennia should be merged with Arthropterygius or kept as a separate genus.
